ਸੰਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਰੇਣੁਕਾ ਲੈ ਮਾਥੈ ਲਾਵਉ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ:
Applying the dust of the saints' feet to the forehead signifies total humility and the supreme value of sangat (company of the devout). This physical gesture represents obtaining the nine treasures and eighteen spiritual powers, treating the dust of holy feet as the greatest wealth and ultimate spiritual attainment.

Themes: humility, sangat, dust of feet, spiritual wealth, surrender, nine treasures, eighteen siddhis, reverence.
ਗੁਰਸਿਖਾਂ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਧੂੜਿ ਦੇਹਿ ਹਮ ਪਾਪੀ ਭੀ ਗਤਿ:
The speaker pleads for the dust of the Guru's Sikhs' feet to attain salvation and a high spiritual state. This request for the dust of holy feet symbolizes a desperate desire for sangat (company of the devout) to purify a corrupted soul. The sinner seeks redemption through humble submission to the spiritual status of the devout.
Themes: humility, sangat (company of the devout), redemption, dust of feet, spiritual elevation, divine grace, purification, sin.
ਕਰਉ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਭਗਤ ਜਨ ਧੂਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਲਾਵਉ ॥੩॥:
Expressing radical humility, the speaker bows to devotees and applies the dust of their feet to the face, seeking to join the sangat (company of the devout). This physical gesture of surrender represents a desire to associate with the holy and participate in singing divine virtues. The act transforms reverence into active participation in worship, prioritizing the company of the faithful over ego.

Themes: humility, sangat, devotees, surrender, divine praise, association, worship, ego
ਟਹਲ ਕਰਉ ਤੇਰੇ ਦਾਸ ਕੀ ਪਗ ਝਾਰਉ ਬਾਲ ॥:
The speaker engages in humble service for the Lord's devotee, wiping dust from their feet with hair to manifest total surrender and the destruction of ego. This gesture asserts that serving a true servant of the Divine equals serving the Divine itself, embodying selfless devotion and the rejection of pride through physical abasement.

Themes: Sewa (selfless service), humility, devotee, surrender, ego-erasure, physical abasement, divine connection.
ਕਰਿ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਧੂਰਿ ਦੇਹੁ ਸੰਤਨ ਕੀ ਸੁਖੁ ਨਾਨਕੁ ਇ:
A plea asks for divine grace to grant the dust of the saints' feet, symbolizing extreme humility and the desire for refuge in the sangat. This request yearns for the deep peace obtained through the sanctifying dust of the holy, highlighting that true spiritual comfort lies in the company of the enlightened.

Themes: Divine grace, humility, dust of feet, sangat, spiritual peace, surrender, sanctification.
ਸੰਤਹ ਚਰਣ ਹਮਾਰੋ ਮਾਥਾ ਨੈਨ ਦਰਸੁ ਤਨਿ ਧੂਰਿ ਪਰ:
The speaker pleads for absolute physical surrender to the sangat (company of the devout), desiring that the forehead constantly bow at the lotus feet, the gaze remain fixed on the holy sight, and the body be covered in the dust of the saints. This expresses a yearning for total humility and refuge through prostration before enlightened beings, seeking to merge with the divine through the gateway of the holy congregation.

Themes: sangat, humility, surrender, darshan, prostration, dust of feet, refuge, physical devotion
ਅਤਿ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਮਨਮੋਹਨ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਸਭਹੂ ਮਧਿ ਨਿਰਾਰੇ ॥:
The speaker addresses the supremely beautiful Beloved who captivates the mind, declaring that the Divine exists pervasively within all beings while remaining uniquely distinct and transcendent. Uttering these praises of the enchanting Lord bestows spiritual life. This proclamation celebrates the paradox of the Creator being simultaneously immanent in the world and separate from it.

Themes: Divine beauty, immanence and transcendence, paradox of presence, spiritual nourishment through praise, captivation of the mind.
ਤੇਰਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਰੂੜੋ ਰੂਪੁ ਰੂੜੋ ਅਤਿ ਰੰਗ ਰੂੜੋ ਮੇ:
The devotee ecstatically praises the supreme beauty of the Lord's naam (divine Name), physical form, and deep spiritual love. This declaration of adoration asserts that every aspect of the Beloved is profoundly attractive and perfect. It functions as an intimate outpouring of love, celebrating the aesthetic and spiritual splendor of the Divine.
Themes: Divine beauty, praise of naam, spiritual love, adoration, aesthetic splendor, intimate connection.
ਸੁੰਦਰ ਰਸਾਲ ਤੂ ॥੧॥:
Directly addressing the Divine as beautiful and the origin of all essences, this praises the Lord's aesthetic perfection and role as the fountain of spiritual nectar. It declares that God is the source of all flavors, the essence of existence, and the wellspring of every pleasurable taste.

Themes: Divine beauty, spiritual nectar, source of essence, aesthetic perfection, origin of flavors, praise, adoration.
ਨੈਣ ਪਸੰਦੋ ਸੋਇ ਪੇਖਿ ਮੁਸਤਾਕ ਭਈ ॥:
The sight of the Divine Lord is supremely pleasing to the eyes, and simply beholding Him plunges the soul into a state of spiritual intoxication and ecstasy. This declaration of love describes how the vision of the Beloved enraptures the mind, causing a blissful absorption that transcends ordinary consciousness through the power of darshan (divine sight).

Themes: divine beauty, spiritual intoxication, darshan, ecstatic love, visual devotion, absorption in the Beloved, divine attraction.
ਸੁੰਦਰ ਸੋਭਾ ਲਾਲ ਗੋਪਾਲ ਦਇਆਲ ਕੀ ਅਪਰ ਅਪਾਰਾ ਰ:
Praises the beautiful, infinite glory of the merciful Lord of the Universe, Gopal, stating that His splendor pervades the realm of compassion. Declares the Divine's magnificence to be boundless and without end, highlighting the connection between His limitless nature and His role as the compassionate sustainer. The text celebrates the vastness of the Beloved's presence.
Themes: Divine glory, infinite nature, mercy, praise, boundlessness, beauty, Gopal, compassion.
ਅਪੁਨੇ ਸੇਵਕ ਕੀ ਆਪੇ ਰਾਖੈ ਆਪੇ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਵੈ ॥:
The Divine personally safeguards the honor and existence of His own devotees while acting as the inner force that inspires and enables their practice of simran (loving remembrance). This asserts that spiritual protection and the chanting of naam (the divine Name) are gifts granted by the Creator rather than human achievements, emphasizing total dependence on divine grace for both preservation and devotion.
Themes: Divine protection, grace, simran, naam, divine agency, devotee, surrender, preservation
ਭਗਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਜੀਉ ਰਾਖੈ ਜੁਗਿ ਜੁਗਿ ਰਖਦਾ ਆ:
The Beloved preserves the honor and safety of His humble servants across all time. This declaration affirms that the Divine maintains the dignity of devotees throughout every age, consistently shielding them from dishonor or harm. God has historically upheld the respect of those who surrender.

Themes: Divine protection, preservation of honor, devotees, timelessness, historical continuity, God's care, humility
ਭਗਤ ਤੇਰੇ ਸਭਿ ਪ੍ਰਾਣਪਤਿ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਮ ਤੂੰ ਭਗਤਨ ਕਾ:
Addressing the Divine as the Master of life and the Beloved, this declaration establishes a mutual affection where the devotee is dear to God and God is dear to the devotee. It affirms the reciprocal nature of the relationship between the Lord and the bhagat (devotee), emphasizing that the spiritual bond is one of shared love and intimacy rather than distant worship.

Themes: Reciprocal love, Divine intimacy, bhagat (devotee), Master of life, mutual affection, spiritual relationship, Beloved Lord.
ਭਗਤਾ ਕੀ ਟੇਕ ਤੂੰ ਸੰਤਾ ਕੀ ਓਟ ਤੂੰ ਸਚਾ ਸਿਰਜਨ:
Addressing the eternal Creator, the text declares that the divine Name (naam) serves as the sole reliance and refuge for devotees and saints. The Divine acts as the physical support and protective shelter for the devout. This praise establishes the Creator as the ultimate sanctuary where the faithful find stability.

Themes: divine support, refuge in naam, protection of saints, creator as sanctuary, reliance on god, devotee's stability
ਹਰਿ ਜੁਗੁ ਜੁਗੁ ਭਗਤ ਉਪਾਇਆ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਦਾ ਆਇਆ ਰਾਮ:
The Divine creates bhagats (devotees) in every age and actively preserves their honor, particularly during times of adversity. This eternal protection ensures that the dignity of the faithful remains intact regardless of the era. God sustains the respect of his servants across all time.

Themes: Divine protection, preservation of honor, eternal devotees, God as sustainer, dignity in adversity, creation of the faithful.
ਹਮਰੇ ਕਰਮ ਨ ਬਿਚਰਹੁ ਠਾਕੁਰ ਤੁਮ੍ਹ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਹੁ ਅ:
The soul pleads with the Divine Master to disregard all past deeds and preserve the servant's dignity. This prayer for unconditional grace asserts that salvation depends on God's protection rather than personal merit or karma, emphasizing total surrender and the preservation of honor through divine will alone.

Themes: karma, divine grace, surrender, servitude, divine protection, mercy, unconditional acceptance.
ਜਾਚਿਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਨਿਤ ਨਾਮੁ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਕਰੇ ਕਬੂਲੁ ॥:
The human acts as a beggar pleading for naam (the divine Name), and the Master accepts this request. This instruction encourages humility by framing the seeker as a supplicant who must ask for spiritual wealth rather than material gain. The Lord grants the gift of loving remembrance to those who persistently request it.

Themes: begging, divine Name, Master, acceptance, humility, spiritual wealth, supplication
ਦੇਹਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਸੰਤੋਖੀਆ ਉਤਰੈ ਮਨ ਕੀ ਭੁਖ ॥:
A prayer requests the divine gift of naam to generate true contentment and extinguish the mind's insatiable hunger. The speaker seeks the cessation of inner craving through the bestowal of the Name, linking spiritual satisfaction directly to divine grace. This plea identifies the remedy for mental thirst as the reception of the divine Name, resulting in a state of complete fulfillment and peace.

Themes: Naam, santokh (contentment), mental hunger, divine grace, cessation of craving, spiritual satisfaction, inner peace.
ਜਾਚਿਕੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਾਚੈ ਜਾਚੈ ॥:
A humble soul repeatedly begs the Divine Master and Giver of all happiness for the gift of naam. This plea emphasizes total dependence on the Lord as the only refuge, portraying the seeker as a beggar who continuously asks for spiritual wealth rather than material gain.

Themes: humility, divine naam, begging, dependence, divine master, refuge, spiritual wealth
ਕਰਹੁ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਗੋਪਾਲ ਗੋਬਿਦੇ ਅਪਨਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਵਹ:
A plea requests divine grace to enable the chanting of naam, acknowledging that spiritual practice depends entirely on the Sustainer's support. The speaker asks the Lord of the Universe to grant the capacity for simran, emphasizing that loving remembrance is a gift from the Creator rather than a self-generated act. This humble petition seeks assistance to meditate on the divine Name.

Themes: Divine grace, chanting naam, simran, humble petition, dependency on God, spiritual assistance, meditation.
ਜਾਚਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਦਾਨੁ ਦੇਹਿ ਪਿਆਰਿਆ ॥:
Identifying the self as a beggar, the devotee pleads with the Beloved Lord for the gift of the limitless Shabad (divine Word). This request frames spiritual wisdom as the only true charity worth seeking. The soul asks for the treasure of Naam, acknowledging dependence on divine grace rather than material wealth.

Themes: Beggar, Divine charity, Shabad (divine Word), Beloved, Spiritual wealth, Humility, Dependence on grace
ਦਰਿ ਮੰਗਤੁ ਜਾਚੈ ਦਾਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਦੀਜੈ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਕਰਿ:
The speaker adopts the humble posture of a beggar at the Divine door to request a spiritual gift, emphasizing total dependence on the Lord's mercy rather than personal merit. This plea for charity acknowledges spiritual emptiness and the necessity of grace, framing the devotee as entirely reliant on the benevolence of the Creator for sustenance and salvation.

Themes: Divine mercy, spiritual begging, humility, grace, dependence on God, surrender, seeking refuge.
ਮਉਲਿਓ ਮਨੁ ਤਨੁ ਹੋਇਓ ਹਰਿਆ ਏਕ ਬੂੰਦ ਜਿਨਿ ਪਾਈ:
The mind blooms and the body becomes lush green upon tasting a single drop of the divine Nectar, identified as naam (the divine Name). This metaphor illustrates total spiritual revitalization, where the entire being flourishes and finds new life through even the slightest connection to the divine essence.
Themes: naam (the divine Name), spiritual nectar, blossoming of the mind, bodily revitalization, transformation, divine grace, abundance, spiritual awakening.
ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਤ ਸਦ ਹੀ ਰਾਤਾ ॥:
Drinking the Lord's essence, identified as the nectar of naam, permanently dyes the human consciousness in divine color. This internal consumption causes a perpetual saturation, leaving the devotee forever imbued and colored by the spiritual flavor of the Creator, resulting in a state of constant transformation and absorption.

Themes: Naam, amrit, spiritual intoxication, permanent transformation, divine absorption, internal consumption, coloring of the mind.
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਰਸੁ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਗਾਈਐ ਅਹਿਨਿਸਿ ਪੂਰਨ:
Singing the Lord's kirtan (sacred hymns) provides the amrit (immortal nectar) that sustains spiritual life. This act of worship generates an unceasing internal resonance of celestial sound, causing the naad (divine sound current) to vibrate within the being day and night. The text instructs devotees to chant praises to experience perpetual inner bliss.
Themes: kirtan, amrit, naad, celestial sound, continuous worship, inner bliss, spiritual sustenance, divine resonance.
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਰਸਨਾ ਪੀਉ ਪਿਆਰੀ ॥:
Addressing the tongue as a beloved companion, this instruction commands it to consume the essence of the divine Name, which grants spiritual vitality. The speaker urges the physical organ to taste the immortalizing nectar of naam, transforming speech into a source of soul-nourishment rather than worldly indulgence.

Themes: tongue, naam, amrit, spiritual nourishment, internal instruction, speech, divine essence
ਤੇਰਾ ਜਨੁ ਰਾਮ ਰਸਾਇਣਿ ਮਾਤਾ ॥:
The devotee remains spiritually intoxicated, completely absorbed in the bliss of the Lord's naam (divine Name). This state of divine inebriation signifies a total loss of self in the sublime essence of the Beloved, where the servant is perpetually drunk on the taste of spiritual nectar.

Themes: spiritual intoxication, divine absorption, naam (divine Name), ecstatic devotion, spiritual nectar, self-effacement, divine bliss
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਆ ਗੁਰ ਸਬਦੀ ਹਮ ਨਾਮ ਵਿਟਹੁ ਕ:
Drinking the ambrosial nectar of naam (the divine Name) via the Guru’s word bestows spiritual vitality. The devotee proclaims having imbibed this essence and offers themselves as a sacrifice to the Divine Name. This internal experience of tasting immortality compels an outward act of total self-abnegation and loving surrender.

Themes: divine Name, Guru's word, spiritual nectar, self-surrender, sacrifice, internal consumption, immortality.
ਰਸੁ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਰਸੁ ਅਤਿ ਭਲਾ ਕਿਤੁ ਬਿਧਿ:
The divine Name (Naam) is the supreme nectar granting spiritual life, surpassing all other flavors. This plea seeks the method to consume and internalize this ambrosial essence. The speaker yearns to taste the ultimate spiritual sustenance, asking how a human being can obtain this immortalizing flavor of the Creator.

Themes: Naam, Amrit, spiritual sustenance, yearning for union, internalization of the divine, method of realization, supreme essence.
ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥:
The speaker urges the listener to spiritually consume the divine essence, using the metaphor of drinking to signify internalizing the Lord's flavor. This instruction directs the mind to practice simran, or loving remembrance, by chanting the Name while taking refuge in the Guru. It is an exhortation to fully imbibe and become saturated with the Supreme Being's presence through devotional absorption.

Themes: divine essence, spiritual consumption, naam (divine Name), simran (loving remembrance), Guru's refuge, internalization of the Lord, divine flavor.
ਬਿਖੈ ਬਨੁ ਫੀਕਾ ਤਿਆਗਿ ਰੀ ਸਖੀਏ ਨਾਮੁ ਮਹਾ ਰਸੁ:
The speaker urges the mind to abandon the insipid water of worldly passions and attachments, choosing instead to imbibe the supreme nectar of naam (the divine Name). This plea contrasts spiritual emptiness with the profound satisfaction found in loving remembrance, instructing the soul to reject corruption for the essence of the Divine.

Themes: worldly passions, divine Name, spiritual nourishment, rejection of corruption, nectar of immortality, inner satisfaction, detachment, simran.
ਕਬੀਰ ਬਿਰਹੁ ਭੁਯੰਗਮੁ ਮਨਿ ਬਸੈ ਮੰਤੁ ਨ ਮਾਨੈ ਕ:
The serpent of separation from the Divine coils within the mind, rendering all mantras (sacred incantations) ineffective. This intense longing for the Beloved cannot be subdued by ritual words or magic formulas. The imagery of a poisonous snake illustrates the consuming nature of spiritual anguish, which remains untouched by external religious practices and demands a deeper connection.

Themes: separation from Divine, spiritual longing, futility of mantras, inner anguish, metaphor of snake, mind's condition.
ਹਰਿ ਬਿਨੁ ਕਿਉ ਜੀਵਾ ਮੇਰੀ ਮਾਈ ॥:
Addressing the mother, the speaker laments that life is restless and impossible without the naam (divine Name). This plea expresses total dependence on the Supreme Soul, declaring existence unbearable without spiritual connection. The rhetorical question emphasizes the futility of living separated from the Divine.

Themes: mother, naam, spiritual restlessness, existential dependence, separation from God, lament, impossibility of life.
ਪ੍ਰਭ ਮਿਲਬੇ ਕਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਮਨਿ ਲਾਗੀ ॥:
The mind has become attached with love for the sole purpose of meeting the Divine. An intense longing for union with the Beloved has awakened internally, shifting focus entirely toward spiritual connection. This attachment signifies a deep, transformative yearning for the Supreme Being, declaring that the heart is now fixed on the goal of divine union.
Themes: Divine union, spiritual longing, love for God, internal awakening, attachment to the Divine, yearning for the Beloved.
ਹਰਿ ਦਰਸਨ ਕਉ ਮੇਰਾ ਮਨੁ ਬਹੁ ਤਪਤੈ ਜਿਉ ਤ੍ਰਿਖਾ:
The mind burns with intense longing for the Divine's darshan (sight of the Divine), suffering like a person dying of thirst without water. This simile expresses the soul's desperate need for the Lord's presence, illustrating that separation from God causes unbearable spiritual thirst and agony comparable to physical dehydration.

Themes: Spiritual thirst, Divine darshan, longing for God, separation from the Divine, simile of thirst, burning desire, soul's agony
ਬਾਝਹੁ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਕੋਇ ਨ ਸਾਰੇ ਏਕਲੜੀ ਕੁਰਲਾਏ ॥:
Apart from the Divine Beloved, no one inquires about the soul's welfare, leaving the individual to cry out alone in the wilderness of the world. This expression of spiritual isolation emphasizes that worldly relationships are meaningless without the connection to the Lord-Husband. The soul laments its separation, realizing that only the Creator truly cares for existence.

Themes: spiritual isolation, separation from God, world as wilderness, soul-bride lament, Divine Beloved, futility of worldly relations, crying out
ਮਨਿ ਬੈਰਾਗੁ ਭਇਆ ਦਰਸਨੁ ਦੇਖਣੈ ਕਾ ਚਾਉ ॥:
The mind experiences detachment from worldly existence because love for the Divine has awakened within it. This internal shift creates an intense thirst to behold the Divine presence, known as darshan. The soul now craves the sight of the Beloved above all else, having lost interest in material concerns due to this overwhelming affection.

Themes: detachment, divine love, darshan, spiritual longing, worldly detachment, thirst for the divine, internal transformation
ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਚਿਰੀ ਵਿਛੁੰਨਿਆ ਮਿਲੁ ਸਬਦਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਪ੍:
The soul pleads with the Divine Husband to enter the heart-home and end ages of separation. This urgent petition seeks spiritual union through the Guru's Shabad (divine instruction). The devotee invites the Lord to dwell within, curing the pain of long estrangement by merging with the divine Word.

Themes: Divine union, spiritual longing, Guru's Shabad, heart as sanctuary, separation from God, divine marriage, invitation to the Lord
ਪਿਰ ਦੋਸੁ ਨਾਹੀ ਸੁਖਹ ਦਾਤੇ ਹਉ ਵਿਛੁੜੀ ਬੁਰਿਆਰ:
The soul exonerates the Divine Husband, acknowledging Him as the source of all peace while blaming personal bad deeds for their spiritual separation. This confession accepts full responsibility for the distance from the Giver of comfort, asserting that the Lord is blameless. By attributing the rift to one's own negative actions, the speaker pleads for reunion while praising the Lord's perfection.

Themes: Divine perfection, human error, spiritual separation, personal responsibility, bad karma, Lord as Husband.
ਆਉ ਜੀ ਤੂ ਆਉ ਹਮਾਰੈ ਹਰਿ ਜਸੁ ਸ੍ਰਵਨ ਸੁਨਾਵਨਾ:
The speaker pleads with the Beloved Guru to enter and reside within the heart as a home, requesting that the ears be filled with the Lord's praises. This urgent invitation seeks divine indwelling and the ability to perceive the Creator's glory through hearing. It expresses deep longing for the Guru's presence to transform the inner self into a sanctuary for listening to divine virtues.

Themes: Invitation to the Guru, heart as a divine home, hearing the Lord's praises, longing for presence, inner sanctuary, spiritual listening.
ਆਉ ਹਮਾਰੈ ਰਾਮ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਜੀਉ ॥:
An intimate invitation for the Divine Beloved to physically come and permanently reside within the heart, expressing a desperate longing for internal union. This plea asks the Lord to inhabit the mind, transforming the devotee through constant presence. It is a direct call for the Beloved to take up residence within the soul.

Themes: Divine union, internal residence, intimate longing, invitation to the Beloved, heart as sanctuary, spiritual presence.
ਬਿਨਵੰਤਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਦਇਆ ਧਾਰਹੁ ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਨਾਹ ਪਿਆਰ:
The soul-bride pleads for divine mercy and asks the Beloved Husband to reside within the heart-home. This intimate petition seeks grace and union, framing the body as a dwelling for the Lord. It expresses deep longing for the Divine presence to inhabit the self.

Themes: soul-bride, divine husband, mercy, heart-home, union, longing, grace, divine presence.
ਮੋਹਨ ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਕਰਉ ਜੋਦਰੀਆ ॥:
A fervent plea invites the Fascinating Lord to enter and reside within the home of the heart. The devotee asks the Beloved to take up permanent residence inside the body, transforming the physical self into a divine abode through intimate presence. This request seeks internal union and the occupation of the mind by the Enchanter.

Themes: Divine invitation, heart as abode, internal residence, longing for union, prayerful request, intimate presence, spiritual habitation.
ਹਮ ਘਰਿ ਸਾਜਨ ਆਏ ॥:
The Divine Beloved has manifested within the heart-home, transforming the internal self into a dwelling for the Lord. This proclamation celebrates the arrival of the Friend-God inside the devotee, signifying deep spiritual union and the presence of the Creator within the body. The heart becomes the residence where the Master appears.

Themes: Divine union, internalization of God, heart as temple, manifestation of the Lord, spiritual arrival, presence of the Beloved.
ਪਹਿਲੈ ਪਹਰੈ ਫੁਲੜਾ ਫਲੁ ਭੀ ਪਛਾ ਰਾਤਿ ॥:
Devotion performed in the early watches of the night is beautiful like a flower, but the substantial fruit of spiritual realization comes only during the amrit vela, the ambrosial hour before dawn. This metaphor distinguishes between the aesthetic pleasure of initial worship and the consummate reward found in the final, most sacred time of prayer.

Themes: amrit vela, spiritual progression, early devotion, worship timing, metaphor of flowers and fruit, night watches, spiritual reward
ਕਬੀਰ ਸੂਤਾ ਕਿਆ ਕਰਹਿ ਉਠਿ ਕਿ ਨ ਜਪਹਿ ਮੁਰਾਰਿ:
Wasting human life intoxicated by maya (worldly attachment) is condemned as spiritual sleep. The voice admonishes the self to awaken from this lethargy and engage in simran (loving remembrance) of the Supreme Being. Instead of remaining lost in illusion, one must rise and meditate on the Divine. This urgent plea contrasts the stupor of attachment with the alertness required for devotion.

Themes: Spiritual awakening, maya (worldly attachment), simran (loving remembrance), wasting human life, self-admonition, spiritual lethargy, divine meditation
ਪਰਭਾਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਗੁਰ ਕੇ ਚਰਣ ਧਿਆਇ ॥:
Rise during the amrit vela, the nectar time before dawn, to engage in simran, the loving remembrance of the Divine. Focus the mind on the Guru's feet, a concrete image representing total surrender and the internalization of the teacher's guidance. This directive commands a daily discipline of chanting the divine Name while fixing the Guru's reverence within the heart.

Themes: Amrit vela, simran, Guru's feet, surrender, daily discipline, divine Name, reverence, internalization
ਝਾਲਾਘੇ ਉਠਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਨਿਸਿ ਬਾਸੁਰ ਆਰਾਧਿ ॥:
Wake up during the ambrosial hour to chant the divine Name, then maintain continuous loving remembrance of the Lord day and night. This instruction commands the devotee to begin spiritual practice at dawn and sustain worship and adoration ceaselessly, ensuring the mind remains connected to the Creator at all times.
Themes: Amrit Vela, Naam, continuous remembrance, spiritual discipline, dawn meditation, unbroken worship.
ਬਾਬੀਹਾ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਵੇਲੈ ਬੋਲਿਆ ਤਾਂ ਦਰਿ ਸੁਣੀ ਪ:
The rainbird cries out during the ambrosial pre-dawn hours, and its plea is accepted within the Divine Court. This illustrates that intense longing offered at the sacred time of amrit vela reaches the Creator directly, ensuring that sincere devotion is heard and answered by the Sovereign.
Themes: rainbird, amrit vela, divine court, prayer, longing, acceptance, divine hearing
ਛਾਤੀ ਸੀਤਲ ਮਨੁ ਸੁਖੀ ਛੰਤ ਗੋਬਿਦ ਗੁਨ ਗਾਇ ॥:
Singing the Glorious Praises of the Lord of the Universe cools the burning heart and brings peace to the mind. Devotional singing extinguishes inner fire and creates mental tranquility through the glorification of the Divine. This practice transforms emotional agitation into a state of spiritual comfort and happiness.
Themes: singing praises, cooling the heart, peace of mind, Divine attributes, emotional healing, devotional music, tranquility.
ਜੋਗੁ ਬਨਿਆ ਤੇਰਾ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਗਾਈ ॥੧॥:
Singing the divine praises, or kirtan, bestows the state of yoga, representing perfect union with the Divine. This devotional act grants both worldly fulfillment and the peace of renunciation, transcending duality. The speaker declares that true spiritual discipline and connection are realized solely through the musical glorification of the Creator’s virtues.

Themes: kirtan, spiritual union, yoga, divine praise, devotional singing, transcendence of duality, fulfillment
ਹਉ ਅਨਦਿਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਕਰਉ ॥:
The devotee pledges unceasing worship by singing kirtan (musical praise) of the divine Name (naam) night and day. This constant remembrance transforms time into a continuous offering of adoration, signifying a life wholly surrendered to the rhythmic repetition of God’s virtues and eternal presence.
Themes: constant remembrance, kirtan, divine Name, unceasing devotion, singing praises, time as worship.
ਰੁਣ ਝੁਣੋ ਸਬਦੁ ਅਨਾਹਦੁ ਨਿਤ ਉਠਿ ਗਾਈਐ ਸੰਤਨ ਕ:
Rise early daily to join the sangat (company of the devout) and sing the unstruck celestial sound, which is the sweet musical praise of the Divine. This directive commands vocalizing the Bani with one uniform flavor of absorption, merging with the divine melody through the company of the holy.
Themes: Amrit Vela, sangat, kirtan, anahad nad, divine praise, daily discipline, absorption.
ਸਾਧੋ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਕੇ ਗੁਨ ਗਾਵਉ ॥:
Addressing devout saints, this imperative commands the continuous singing of the Divine Sustainer's virtues. It instructs the holy congregation to engage in perpetual glorification through vocal praise, establishing that the essence of saintly life is the ceaseless adoration of the Creator's qualities. The act functions as a call to maintain constant remembrance and celebrate the attributes of the Universal Lord.

Themes: praise of the Divine, saintly conduct, glorification of Gobind, vocal remembrance, devotional instruction, divine attributes, continuous worship.
ਨਿਰਬਾਣ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਗਾਵਹੁ ਕਰਤੇ ਕਾ ਨਿਮਖ ਸਿਮਰਤ ਜ:
Sing the Creator's praises while free of latent desires, for even a moment of simran (loving remembrance) liberates the soul from vices. This instruction links the state of desirelessness with devotional singing, promising that instant meditation on the divine Name frees one from inner corruptions and grants ultimate salvation.

Themes: Nirvana, kirtan, liberation from vices, simran, desirelessness, divine praise, instant salvation.
ਮਨ ਮੀਠ ਤੁਹਾਰੋ ਕੀਓ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥:
The mind finds total sweetness in every action of the Divine, expressing complete acceptance of the divine will (hukam) and satisfaction with all circumstances. This profound contentment results in never blaming others or complaining about worldly troubles, as the devotee perceives all events as the Creator's benevolent doing rather than human fault.

Themes: Hukam, Divine Will, Acceptance, Contentment, Non-blame, Surrender, Sweetness, Trust
ਮੀਤ ਕੇ ਕਰਤਬ ਕੁਸਲ ਸਮਾਨਾ ॥੧॥:
The devotee perceives the Divine Friend's every action as pure comfort and delight. This stance of total surrender accepts God's will as inherently benevolent, finding satisfaction in all circumstances. It affirms that the Beloved's deeds are always pleasing, reflecting a deep trust in the Creator's plan.
Themes: Divine Will, acceptance, friendship with God, surrender, trust, benevolence
ਸਰਬ ਸੁਖ ਆਨੰਦ ਮੰਗਲ ਰਸ ਮਾਨਿ ਗੋਬਿੰਦੈ ਆਗਿਓ ॥:
Accepting the sweet will (raza) of the Lord of the Universe brings total peace, joy, and auspiciousness. By acknowledging the Divine pleasure, the devotee experiences every form of bliss and spiritual nectar. This declaration affirms that surrender to the Creator’s order results in complete happiness and the arrival of all desirable qualities.

Themes: Divine will, surrender, acceptance, bliss, peace, auspiciousness, spiritual nectar, divine pleasure.
ਖਿਨ ਮਹਿ ਥਾਪਿ ਉਥਾਪਨਹਾਰਾ ਆਪਨ ਹਾਥਿ ਮਤਾਤ ॥੧॥:
The Divine instantly creates and destroys, holding all decisions and matters within His own hands. This declaration asserts absolute sovereignty over existence, demonstrating that the Creator alone possesses the power to establish and dismantle the world in a single moment, emphasizing total control over every outcome.

Themes: divine sovereignty, creation and destruction, absolute control, divine will, transient existence, omnipotence, divine authority.
ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਈਐ ਕਾਰਜੁ ਆਵੈ ਰਾਸਿ ॥੧॥:
Establishing the divine Name (naam) within the mind guarantees that every worldly undertaking reaches its successful conclusion. Constant remembrance resolves all difficulties and brings affairs to a fruitful end. This instruction asserts that spiritual focus secures practical outcomes.

Themes: Naam meditation, worldly success, divine resolution, spiritual focus, practical outcomes, remembrance.
ਕਾਰਜੁ ਤੇਰਾ ਹੋਵੈ ਪੂਰਾ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਗੁਣ ਗਾਇ:
Directing the mind to chant the Name of Hari ensures that all tasks and endeavors reach successful completion. Singing the virtues of the Divine guarantees the fulfillment of one's duties. Instructing the self to engage in constant praise leads to the perfect resolution of all affairs through the grace of the Creator.

Themes: success of endeavors, chanting Hari, instruction to the mind, divine will, fulfillment of duties, singing virtues, kirtan, grace
ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਅਰਾਧਣਾ ਕਾਰਜੁ ਆਵੈ ਰਾਸਿ ॥੮॥:
Engaging in the worship of naam, the divine Name, resolves all worldly tasks and fulfills the ultimate purpose of life. Through the practice of simran, or loving remembrance, every objective is accomplished and spiritual satisfaction is attained. This teaching asserts that focusing on the Divine brings success to all human endeavors and completes the soul's mission.

Themes: naam, simran, resolution of affairs, life purpose, spiritual success, worship, divine satisfaction, accomplishment.
ਸਭੇ ਕਾਜ ਸਵਾਰਿਐ ਜਾ ਤੁਧੁ ਭਾਵੰਦਾ ॥੭॥:
All worldly and spiritual tasks are perfectly arranged and resolved solely through the alignment with the Divine Will, or when the Divine is pleased. This declaration asserts that external success and internal peace depend entirely on the Creator's satisfaction rather than personal effort. The state of having one's affairs settled is the direct fruit of pleasing the Beloved.

Themes: Divine Will, resolution of affairs, surrender, grace, dependence on God, alignment with the Creator.
ਸਗਲ ਮਨੋਰਥ ਪੂਰਨ ਹੋਏ ਕਦੇ ਨ ਹੋਇ ਦੁਖਾਲਾ ਜੀਉ:
All wishes are completely satisfied, resulting in permanent freedom from pain and grief. Every requirement is fulfilled, ensuring that suffering never returns. This state of total contentment banishes anguish forever, signifying that the soul has found ultimate completion and is liberated from the distress of worldly lack.

Themes: fulfillment of desires, cessation of sorrow, spiritual contentment, liberation from suffering, divine grace, completion
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਆਧਾਰੁ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਆਸਰਾ ॥:
The beautiful lotus feet of the Divine serve as the ultimate foundation and refuge for the lives of devotees. Humble servants find their anchor and support in the Lord's feet, declaring that spiritual stability relies completely on seeking shelter in the Divine presence.

Themes: Divine support, lotus feet, refuge, sanctuary, devotee reliance, spiritual foundation, divine protection.
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸੇਵੀ ਰਿਦ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਗੁਰ ਪੂਰੇ ਕੈ ਆਧਾਰਿ:
Anchoring the mind in the heart through the refuge of the Perfect Guru allows for constant internal worship of the Divine's lotus feet. This act of surrender fixes loving remembrance of the Lord's beautiful presence within the self, relying entirely on the complete teacher's support to sustain this spiritual connection.

Themes: Divine refuge, internal worship, Guru's support, lotus feet, heart-centered meditation, surrender, spiritual anchoring, loving remembrance.
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸਿਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਰੀਤਿ ਸੰਤਨ ਮਨਿ ਆਵਏ ਜੀਉ:
The established discipline of cherishing the Divine's lotus feet occupies the minds of the saints. This custom of loving surrender and reverence toward the Supreme Being dwells permanently within their consciousness. True spiritual existence is defined by this continuous practice of devotion and the internalization of divine etiquette.

Themes: Divine love, lotus feet, spiritual discipline, sant, surrender, consciousness, devotion, maryada
ਬੋਹਿਥੜਾ ਹਰਿ ਚਰਣ ਮਨ ਚੜਿ ਲੰਘੀਐ ॥:
The mind is commanded to board the Lord's lotus feet, which function as a beautiful vessel to ferry the soul across the terrifying ocean of worldly existence. By taking refuge in the Divine, one escapes the cycle of reincarnation and reaches the far shore of liberation, using total surrender as the only means of safe passage through life's perils.
Themes: Divine refuge, boat metaphor, crossing the world ocean, liberation of the soul, instruction to the mind, surrender, lotus feet.
ਹਰਿ ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਮਨੁ ਬੇਧਿਆ ਕਿਛੁ ਆਨ ਨ ਮੀਠਾ ਰਾਮ:
The mind is pierced by the lotus feet of the Divine, symbolizing total surrender and the penetration of consciousness by God's presence. Once the mind is fixed on the Lord King, nothing else tastes sweet, meaning all worldly attractions lose their flavor. This state of absorption renders maya (worldly attachment) tasteless, as the devotee finds complete satisfaction only in the remembrance of the Supreme Being.

Themes: divine lotus feet, pierced mind, exclusivity of devotion, loss of worldly taste, surrender, remembrance, supreme satisfaction.
ਪੀ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਆਘਾਨਿਆ ਗੁਰਿ ਅਮਰੁ ਕਰਾਇਆ ॥੨॥:
Drinking the divine nectar satisfies the soul, and the Guru bestows immortality. This declares a state of spiritual elevation free from aging, death, and sorrow. It emphasizes that internalizing divine essence through the Guru's instruction ends the cycle of mortality and suffering.
Themes: divine nectar, spiritual immortality, Guru's instruction, soul satisfaction, freedom from death, cessation of sorrow, eternal life.
ਜਿਨ੍ਹ ਪੀਆ ਸੇ ਮਸਤ ਭਏ ਹੈ ਤੂਟੇ ਬੰਧਨ ਫਾਹੇ ॥:
Consuming the essence of naam (the divine Name) induces spiritual intoxication, instantly severing the chains of maya (worldly attachment). Imbibing this divine nectar breaks every shackle of bondage, liberating the soul into ecstatic union. The act of drinking the divine ambrosia destroys all fetters of existence.

Themes: naam, spiritual intoxication, liberation from maya, breaking shackles, divine nectar, ecstatic union, soul freedom.
ਹਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਸੋ ਚਖੈ ਮੇਰੇ ਮਨਾ ॥੨॥:
The mind is urged to drink the spiritual water of the Lord's Name (Naam), which bestows eternal life. Tasting this divine ambrosia nourishes the soul and provides true sustenance. Consuming the immortalizing essence of Hari-Naam revitalizes the inner self, transforming mere existence into spiritual vitality.

Themes: Naam, amrit, spiritual nourishment, mind, divine sustenance, eternal life, Hari-Naam
ਗੁਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਹਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਚੋਇਆ ਮੇਰੀ ਜਿੰਦੁੜੀ:
The Guru pours the immortal nectar of naam (the divine Name) into the mouth, resurrecting a soul previously dead in spiritual ignorance. This act of divine grace revives the dying self, granting eternal life through the taste of the Lord. The text celebrates the transformation from spiritual death to living awareness caused by the Guru's gift of the Lord's essence.

Themes: Guru's grace, spiritual resurrection, naam (divine Name), immortality, spiritual death, divine nectar, awakening the soul.
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਮਿਲਿ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥:
The divine Name (naam) is identified as an inexhaustible treasure and immortalizing nectar. This instruction urges the listener to gather in the company of the devout (sangat) to consume this spiritual sustenance. It presents the absorption of God's identity as a communal act of drinking a life-giving elixir, framing the Lord's wealth as something to be actively ingested through collective worship.

Themes: Naam, spiritual treasure, amrit (nectar), sangat (congregation), divine sustenance, communal worship, internalization.
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟਿਓਨੁ ਫਿਰਿ ਜੋਨਿ ਨ ਪਾਏ ॥:
Divine grace severs the terror of birth and death, liberating the devotee from the cycle of reincarnation. This declares the cessation of wandering through life forms, as the soul escapes the wheel of transmigration. The fear of mortality is annihilated, ensuring the individual does not return to the physical plane or suffer the anxiety of dying again.

Themes: liberation, reincarnation, fear of death, transmigration, divine grace, cycle of birth and death, cessation of wandering.
ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਜਮ ਕਾ ਭਉ ਲਥਾ ॥੨੦॥:
Achieving sahaj (natural intuitive poise) stabilizes the mind, leading to union with the Divine. This inner stillness destroys the fear of the Messenger of Death, rendering spiritual death powerless. The text declares liberation through mental steadiness and divine realization, where the steady mind meets the Lord and escapes the terror of mortality.

Themes: sahaj, divine union, fear of death, mental steadiness, liberation, messenger of death, intuitive poise, spiritual stability.
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਸਬਦੁ ਜਪਿ ॥:
Reciting hymns of praise within the sangat (company of the devout) severs the terrifying cycle of reincarnation and the dread of mortality. The practice of simran (loving remembrance) through the sabad (divine instruction) cuts away the existential fear of birth and death, liberating the mind from the anxiety of transmigration and the endless cycle of suffering.

Themes: fear of birth and death, sabad, simran, reincarnation cycle, liberation, sangat, praise
ਨ ਦਨੋਤਿ ਜਸਮਰਣੇਨ ਜਨਮ ਜਰਾਧਿ ਮਰਣ ਭਇਅੰ ॥੧॥ ਰ:
Engaging in simran (loving remembrance) dissolves the terror of the life cycle, ensuring that birth, old age, and death cause no suffering. This practice of meditation removes the pain of mortality and the anxiety of existence, liberating the mind from the fear of dying. Constant remembrance transcends the dread of physical decay and the cycle of reincarnation.

Themes: simran, liberation from fear, mortality, cycle of birth and death, transcendence, meditation, anxiety, old age
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਦੁਖੁ ਕਾਟੀਐ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਚੂਕੈ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਕਾਣੇ:
Residing in the sangat (company of the devout) severs the lifelong suffering of birth and death, eradicating the terror of the Messenger of Death. This declaration affirms that spiritual companionship cuts the knot of transmigration and removes all existential dread, liberating the devotee from the fear of dying.

Themes: sangat, transmigration, fear of death, liberation, suffering, spiritual companionship, existential dread
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭੈ ਲਾਥੇ ॥੪॥੨॥੫੨॥:
The primal dread of the cycle of birth and death is entirely extinguished, affirming a state of absolute spiritual fearlessness. All anxiety regarding transmigration and mortality vanishes, signifying liberation from the endless wheel of reincarnation. This confirms that the soul has transcended the fundamental terror of dying and living again through divine connection.

Themes: birth and death, fearlessness, liberation, transmigration, existential dread, cycle of reincarnation, spiritual freedom.
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੈ ਆਸਰੈ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਸਿਉ ਰੰਗੁ ਲਾਏ ॥:
Taking refuge in the sangat (company of the devout) dyes the consciousness in the color of divine love. Relying on the holy congregation fosters deep affection and absorption in the Creator. This communal support enables the soul to merge intimately with the Lord, transforming attachment from the world to the Divine.
Themes: holy congregation, divine love, spiritual refuge, communal support, absorption in God, romantic devotion, transformation through company
ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗਿ ਤਰੀਜੈ ਸਾਗਰੁ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਫਾਸਾ ਜੀ:
Immersion in the holy sangat (company of the devout) allows the soul to traverse the terrifying ocean of worldly existence. This spiritual fellowship severs the fatal noose of the Messenger of Death, liberating the being from the cycle of reincarnation. Associating with the pious provides the means to escape the entrapment of mortality and cross the sea of maya (worldly attachment).

Themes: sangat, liberation, ocean of world, noose of death, maya, spiritual fellowship, transcendence
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੀ ਭੀਰ ਜਉ ਪਾਈ ਤਉ ਨਾਨਕ ਹਰਿ ਸੰਗਿ:
Obtaining the sanctuary of the holy congregation, sangat, causes the ego to dissolve and results in immediate union with the Divine. Finding the company of the devout facilitates a direct meeting with the Supreme Being, merging the individual consciousness with the Lord. This declares that spiritual community is the essential gateway to divine connection.
Themes: sangat (holy congregation), divine union, ego death, spiritual community, sanctuary, meeting the Lord, cause and effect in spirituality.
ਸੰਤਤ ਹੀ ਸਤਸੰਗਤਿ ਸੰਗ ਸੁਰੰਗ ਰਤੇ ਜਸੁ ਗਾਵਤ ਹ:
Devotees permanently reside in the sangat (company of the holy), becoming dyed in the celestial hue of divine love. Immersed in this spiritual color, they continuously sing the praises of the Creator. This defines the state of the holy, showing how association with the devout saturates the soul with devotion and causes it to vibrate with the Lord's glory.

Themes: sangat, divine love, singing praises, spiritual transformation, celestial hue, holy company, devotion
ਕਾਢਿ ਲੀਏ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਆਨ ਬਿਖੈ ਤੇ ਸਾਧਸੰਗਿ ਮਨੁ ਲਾਵ:
The speaker implores the Divine to extract the consciousness from the poison of worldly vice and fix it firmly within the sangat (company of the devout). This plea acknowledges that only God can rescue the mind from corruption and redirect it toward holy association. It frames salvation as a divine act of removal and reattachment, separating the soul from toxic attachments to anchor it in spiritual community.

Themes: Divine rescue, Saadh Sangat, detachment from vice, spiritual redirection, prayer, liberation, toxic attachments.
ਮਹਿਮਾ ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗ ਕੀ ਸੁਨਹੁ ਮੇਰੇ ਮੀਤਾ ॥:
Exhorts friends to listen to the glory of the sangat (congregation of devotees). Proclaims the immense value of the holy gathering. Calls attention to the spiritual magnificence inherent in the Guru's assembly. This declaration elevates the collective company of the devout as the supreme object of praise and attention.

Themes: sangat, holy congregation, spiritual community, divine praise, listening, exaltation, gathering of devotees, Guru's assembly
ਮੇਰਾ ਗੁਰੁ ਪਰਮੇਸਰੁ ਸੁਖਦਾਈ ॥:
The speaker identifies their Guru as the Supreme Being, declaring the teacher to be the very form of the Transcendent Lord. This assertion establishes the divine guide as the sole source of all comfort and tranquility, bestowing true peace upon the devotee. The statement unifies the human guide with the divine reality.

Themes: identity of Guru and God, source of peace, divine comfort, Transcendent Lord, spiritual guide, bestower of tranquility, non-duality.
ਤੁਮ ਦਾਤੇ ਤੁਮ ਪੁਰਖ ਬਿਧਾਤੇ ॥:
The speaker praises the Divine as the sole creator and the generous bestower of all gifts to living beings. It affirms that the all-pervading Lord is the ultimate architect of existence who writes the destiny of every soul. This declaration establishes the Divine as the absolute source of creation and the controller of all fortune.

Themes: Divine generosity, Creator, Architect of Destiny, All-pervading Lord, Absolute Sovereignty, Bestower of Gifts, Affirmation of Divine Attributes.
ਕਰੁਣਾ ਮੈ ਕਿਰਪਾਲ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਨਿਧਿ ਜੀਵਨ ਪਦ ਨਾਨਕ:
Addressing the Merciful One as the very form of kindness and the storehouse of grace, the text asserts that beholding the Divine—darshan, the blessed vision—confers the ultimate spiritual status. This sight of the Lord redeems the soul, granting a life of spiritual elevation and liberation. The infinite mercy of the Divine is the source that transforms human existence into a state of supreme spiritual fulfillment.

Themes: Divine mercy, compassion, darshan (vision of the Divine), spiritual redemption, grace, liberation, divine attributes, transformation.
ਤੂੰ ਭਾਰੋ ਠਾਕੁਰੁ ਗੁਣੀ ਗਹੇਰਾ ॥੨॥:
Addressing the Divine as the Great Lord, the text praises the entity as the absolute repository of all virtues and profound depth. This declaration acknowledges the Lord as the treasure of excellence, filled with immeasurable qualities and a deep, all-encompassing nature. It serves as an affirmation of the Divine's supreme character and the devotee's recognition of His immense spiritual stature.

Themes: Divine Lord, repository of virtues, spiritual depth, treasure of excellence, praise, supreme Master, profound nature.
ਦੇਵਣਹਾਰੁ ਦਾਤਾਰੁ ਕਿਤੁ ਮੁਖਿ ਸਾਲਾਹੀਐ ॥:
The Divine is the ultimate provider who sustains all life with rizq (sustenance), yet no human mouth or language possesses the capacity to fully describe or praise His infinite virtues. This expresses humility and the inadequacy of speech before the boundless generosity of the Creator, acknowledging that His greatness transcends all verbal description.
Themes: Divine generosity, inadequacy of language, humility, infinite virtues, sustenance, rhetorical praise.
ਤੇਰੇ ਕਵਨ ਕਵਨ ਗੁਣ ਕਹਿ ਕਹਿ ਗਾਵਾ ਤੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਗ:
The devotee asks which specific virtues to sing and recount because the Divine is the limitless storehouse of all excellence. This humble praise acknowledges the Supreme Lord as the Master and Sustainer of all, whose qualities are too vast to be fully described through song or speech. The speaker recognizes the Divine as the infinite treasury of merit.

Themes: Infinite virtues, Divine praise, Limitless nature, Humility, Treasury of excellence, Supreme Master.
ਰੇ ਬਉਰੇ ਤੁਹਿ ਘਰੀ ਨ ਰਾਖੈ ਕੋਈ ॥:
Addressing the deluded mind as a madman, this warning declares that at death, no one will permit the soul to linger in the body or home for even an instant. It emphasizes the absolute isolation of dying, the futility of attachment to family, and the transient nature of worldly existence where no one can offer refuge at the final moment.
Themes: death, isolation, transience, admonition, worldly attachment, impermanence, solitude, mortality
ਕਾਹੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਡੋਲਤਾ ਹਰਿ ਮਨਸਾ ਪੂਰਣਹਾਰੁ ॥:
Admonishing the wavering mind to trust the Divine as the fulfiller of all wishes. The speaker rebukes their own mental instability, asserting that God satisfies every longing and hope. Doubt is unnecessary because the Supreme Being grants all desires.

Themes: mind, wavering, divine fulfillment, trust, admonition, desires
ਰੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਭੀ ਭਜੁ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ॥੨॥:
The speaker commands the wandering mind to engage in bhajan (devotional worship) of the Divine Master. It urges the internal faculties to cease distraction and focus entirely on the Lord of the Universe. This imperative instructs the self to practice loving remembrance, transforming the mind from a wanderer into a devotee through constant adoration of the Supreme Being.

Themes: instruction to the mind, bhajan (devotional worship), Gobind (Lord of the Universe), internal discipline, loving remembrance, self-command, divine adoration, cessation of wandering.
ਮਨ ਮੇਰਿਆ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਤੇਰੈ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਬਾਹਰਿ ਵਸਤੁ:
Addressing the mind, the speaker instructs it to recognize that the Divine treasure resides internally rather than in external locations like forests. The command is to cease seeking spiritual fulfillment through outward objects because the source of all comfort is already established within the self. This directive emphasizes introspection over external wandering, identifying the Supreme Being as the inner wealth.

Themes: inner divinity, introspection, Divine treasure, internal God, futility of external search, spiritual wealth, self-realization.
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਤੂ ਕਾਏ ਦੇਖਿ ਭੁਲਾਨਾ ॥:
The speaker admonishes the human mind, lost in the attachment of maya (worldly illusion), to listen carefully. By gazing upon the visible world, the self has strayed from the true path of life and forgotten its purpose. This rebuke questions why the soul wanders in distraction instead of seeking the Divine, effectively asking why looking at material reality causes spiritual amnesia.

Themes: maya, worldly illusion, spiritual admonishment, distraction, forgetting the divine, path of life, material attachment
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਥੀਉ ਰੇਣੁ ਜਿਨੀ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਧਿਆਇਆ ॥:
Addressing the mind as a madman, the text commands listening and becoming dust under the feet of those who practice simran, or loving remembrance of the Divine. This instruction demands extreme humility and submission to the sangat, the company of the devout, as the only path to union with the Lord.
Themes: humility, dust of feet, simran, sangat, divine union, self-admonition, listening.
ਲਖ ਖੁਸੀਆ ਪਾਤਿਸਾਹੀਆ ਜੇ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਨਦਰਿ ਕਰੇਇ:
A single compassionate look from the Satiguru (True Guru) bestows happiness exceeding that of hundreds of thousands of kings. This declaration values divine grace over temporal sovereignty, asserting that spiritual fulfillment outweighs all royal pleasures. The devotee finds supreme bliss not through dominion but through the Guru's merciful gaze, which grants inner peace and joy surpassing worldly rule.

Themes: divine grace, Guru's glance, spiritual sovereignty, inner bliss, royal pleasures, divine favor, supremacy of devotion.
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਇ ਦਇਆਲੁ ਤਾ ਦੁਖੁ ਨ ਜਾਣੀਐ ॥:
When the True Guru becomes merciful, the devotee ceases to perceive suffering as pain, even if it occurs. This grace transforms the experience of hardship so that incoming distress is not felt as anguish. The mind, blessed by the Guru, no longer recognizes affliction as suffering, rendering the individual immune to the sting of worldly misery through a shift in perception.

Themes: Guru's mercy, perception of suffering, spiritual grace, immunity to pain, transformation of distress, acceptance of hardship, divine protection.
ਹਰਿ ਚਉਥੜੀ ਲਾਵ ਮਨਿ ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਹਰਿ ਪਾਇਆ ਬਲਿ:
The fourth circumambulation of the marriage ceremony completes the union, causing the mind to attain sahaj, a state of natural poise and spiritual stability. The soul finds the Lord and surrenders completely. This final stage signifies the achievement of unshakable equipoise and the ultimate realization of the Divine Beloved, where the individual self merges fully with the Universal consciousness.

Themes: fourth lavan, spiritual union, sahaj, divine realization, marriage metaphor, inner peace, ultimate stability, finding the Lord
ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਮਨਾਇ ॥:
Internalizing the True Guru within the heart brings complete fulfillment and peace. This declaration asserts that pleasing the Guru through deep internal residence results in the acquisition of all desired fruits, equating spiritual satisfaction with the realization of every wish.

Themes: True Guru, internalization, heart, fulfillment, peace, pleasing, desire, result.
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਮੇਰਾ ਸਦਾ ਸਹਾਈ ਜਿਨਿ ਦੁਖ ਕਾ ਕਾਟਿਆ:
The Satguru functions as an eternal helper who severs the very root of suffering for those seeking sanctuary. This declaration affirms that the Divine Teacher permanently destroys the source of worldly pain and distress, acting as unending support. By cutting the star of fate or the banner of misery, the Guru provides liberation from anguish.
Themes: Satguru, eradication of suffering, divine support, sanctuary, liberation from pain, cutting the root of ego, eternal help.
ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਮਿਲਣ ਕੀ ਇਹ ਤੇਰੀ ਬਰੀਆ ॥:
This specific human life constitutes the sole opportunity to unite with the Divine Lord of the Universe, urging the listener to recognize the urgency of the present moment. The text warns that this fleeting chance for spiritual union with the Supreme Soul must not be wasted, emphasizing that meeting the Creator is the exclusive purpose of this existence.

Themes: divine union, urgency of human life, spiritual opportunity, meeting the Lord, fleeting moment, purpose of existence, warning against waste, sacred chance
ਪ੍ਰਾਣੀ ਤੂੰ ਆਇਆ ਲਾਹਾ ਲੈਣਿ ॥:
The soul enters human life specifically to harvest spiritual wealth through the divine Name, treating existence as a transaction where the only true profit is realization. This instruction declares that the purpose of birth is to gather the treasure of naam, rejecting material gain in favor of eternal spiritual capital.

Themes: purpose of human life, spiritual profit, naam, divine wealth, material vs spiritual gain, human birth opportunity, spiritual commerce.
ਹਰਿ ਭਗਤਿ ਦ੍ਰਿੜੁ ਮਿਲੁ ਸਾਧ ਨਾਨਕ ਤੇਰੈ ਕਾਮਿ:
Meeting the true Guru establishes unwavering devotion within the heart, serving as the only purposeful action in life. This instruction emphasizes that spiritual connection through the holy company is the sole endeavor that yields true benefit, rendering worldly pursuits futile. The text commands the seeker to internalize divine worship as the essential, practical task for human existence.

Themes: Guru, bhagti (devotional worship), spiritual utility, inner firmness, sangat (holy company), life's purpose, divine connection, practical spirituality.
ਜੀਵਨਾ ਸਫਲ ਜੀਵਨ ਸੁਨਿ ਹਰਿ ਜਪਿ ਜਪਿ ਸਦ ਜੀਵਨਾ:
A human life is only successful when one hears and constantly chants the divine Name, transforming temporary existence into eternal life. This instruction defines the purpose of living as continuous remembrance, promising immortality to those who meditate on the Lord. It equates a fruitful existence with the practice of listening and reciting the divine.

Themes: successful human life, eternal existence, chanting the divine Name, listening to the Lord, immortality through remembrance, purpose of living, continuous meditation.
